cincinnati-music-hall.mobility.1: The ADA Accessibility entrance is located on the southeast side of the building on Elm Street. From here, you will enter the Western & Southern Lobby where you will find the Box Office and two South Elevators that provide easy access to every level of Music Hall, including the Ballroom. A North Concourse Elevator also serves all levels, including the Wilks Studio and Balcony Parlor.
cincinnati-music-hall.mobility.2: Access Ambassadors are available at the southeast entrance on Elm Street. These ambassadors will help you find your way and assist you to your seat. Wheelchairs are available upon request for guests needing assistance from the curb or lobby to their seats.
cincinnati-music-hall.sensory.1: Assistive Listening Devices designed to enhance the sound of performances for guests who are deaf or hard of hearing are available at Guest Services, located at the northeast corner of Music Hall's Lindner Grand Foyer. This new system uses Listen Technologies' next generation of personal listening devices, and its integrated neck loop/lanyard improves the listening experience for T-coil users.
cincinnati-music-hall.chronic.1: First Aid Services are available in the North Concourse on the Orchestra Level. For assistance, speak with Music Hall staff member.
cincinnati-music-hall.mobility.4: Special seating is available for guests unable to transfer out of their wheelchairs or with other special seating needs. When possible, contact the Box Office in advance.
cincinnati-music-hall.chronic.2: Single Unit Restrooms can be found at the following locations: 1241 Elm Street entrance, near the Box Office North side of the Orchestra level of Springer Auditorium South side of the Balcony level of Springer Auditorium West side of the Ballroom
cincinnati-music-hall.chronic.3: For your safety and expedited entry into the Aronoff Center or Music Hall, bag sizes are restricted to 18" x 18" x 8" . Bags exceeding this designated size will not be permitted inside the building. Exceptions can be made if you have a medical necessity. If so, notify a staff member who can assist you.
Is it safe for me to walk through the metal detectors if I have a pacemaker or a metal medical implant?
If you have any concerns, please speak with a staff member at Music Hall or the Aronoff Center, and we will be happy to screen you using another method.
cincinnati-music-hall.mobility.5: A convenient drop-off lane is located in front of Music Hall on Elm Street, near the Box Office and wheelchair-accessible entrance (1241 Elm Street). NOTE: Music Hall does not own or manage the parking facilities listed below. Parking rates are subject to change and are posted at each lot.
cincinnati-music-hall.chronic.4: Our Springer Hall performances do offer an area for nursing mothers. Please speak to a staff member for assistance and access to the location.
cincinnati-music-hall.chronic.5: Service animals are always welcome and should remain on a leash or in a harness at all times. If you plan to bring a service animal to an event, please notify your ticketing services representative at the time of purchase.
cincinnati-music-hall.cognitive.1: MUSIC HALL: You may enter Music Hall anytime beginning one to one-and-one-half hours before the start of an event, depending on the policies of the performance.
Anyone who leaves either building at any time will need to repeat the safety screening to re-enter the venues.
cincinnati-music-hall.chronic.6: We do not stop at any restrooms or take any bathroom breaks during any of our tours. You are encouraged to arrive 15 minutes before your start time to use the restrooms. Outdoor building tour guests should visit the park's public restroom on the Race Street side of Washington Park as indoor restrooms will not be available.
cincinnati-music-hall.mobility.6: Indoor building tours provide some opportunities to sit briefly. Our indoor tour is completely ADA accessible however, please let us know at the time of your reservation if you have trouble climbing minimal stairs.

Our outdoor building tour is a 360 degree walk around the building which is about the length and width of a football field. The route does not go up or down any stairs or hills. Tour guests are expected to stay on their feet the whole time without assistance and there are no opportunities to sit along the tour route.
Cincinnati Music Hall is 100% ADA compliant and the tour path accommodates those in walkers and wheelchairs.
cincinnati-music-hall.cognitive.2: Indoor tours are offered year round while outdoor tours are only offered May - October. It is recommended that guests make a reservation and buy tickets in advance through the Cincinnati Arts Association or Music Hall box offices as space is limited. If space is available, tickets can be purchased the day of the tour. All reservations must be paid for in advance.
